question: Among HOSTS/WCVP-recorded resource hosts of Danaus plexippus, how many are independently supported as high, low, nonhost, or unsubstantiated, and where does this change the confidence of inferred anthropogenic resource geography?

independent_study.citation: Greenstein, Steele & Taylor 2022 PLOS ONE 17 e0269701

primary_source_check: Retrieve original independent quality classifications, preserve exact original plant names and categories with provenance; do not infer from the article abstract.
matching: Exact scientific binomial names and WCVP accepted names only initially, aliases/synonyms require independent taxonomic justification and explicit crosswalk, NEVER genus-only matches.

quality_rules.high: H1-H3 positive evidence of relative high performance
quality_rules.low: L1-L3 documented low performance (some L1 only oviposition), do not reclassify as nonhost

analysis_gate: Report exact classified host-link counts and known introduced-only geography where classification is recoverable. Do NOT extrapolate quality per geography as regionally invariant fact, and do NOT infer quality of unclassified hosts.
non_tautological_test: After classification, compare observed quality-class association with host alien-region breadth conditional on botanical family and taxonomic/source coverage. Do not claim 'deleting poor hosts shrinks range' as new biology.
published_prior_art: The nonhost/low quality distinction and preference-performance mismatch were already demonstrated by Greenstein et al. 2022; only a genuinely novel, conditional spatial biological finding could support a separate ecological paper.
stop: If source archive or classifications cannot be independently verified, no numerical host-quality classification is published and route is held.
